correctness.rationale: For n>=3 and 0<p<q<=infty the singular-value two-coordinate ratio R is between beta=2^(1/q-1/p) and 1. R=1 iff rank one, and R=beta iff singular values equal; this holds for quasi-Banach p<1 too. The first-row projection of a rank-one-free F-linear subspace is injective. Over R, an n-dimensional graph T in odd n must have a real eigenvector, so maximal rank-one-free dimension is 2*floor(n/2), achieved by orthogonal complex-structure J on an even plane; hence c_k real is 1 for k<=2n-2d and beta thereafter. Real beta optimizers are rigid: any graph T has <Tu,u>=0 and ||Tu||=||u||; in odd n, decomposing T into skew part A:U->U and a normal b gives A*A=I-bb*, incompatible with even eigenvalue multiplicities unless b=0. Over C, maximal rank-one-free dimension n-1 (shift graph), while complex polarization of <u,Tu>=0 gives T(U) subset U^perp, so beta-only dimensions <=d; compact Grassmannian ensures strict beta<c_k<1 in n+2..2n-d. Complex d-plane-to-orthogonal-d-plane isometries classify first-beta minimizers. Inspected numerical SVD checker for n3..17 and sample exponent pairs; it checks witnesses only, not all-subspace infima.
